**Chakra UI** — `@chakra-ui/react` (`3.38.0`) layers a token-driven recipe and slot-recipe style system on top of `@ark-ui/react` (`5.40.0`) state-machine primitives and `@emotion/react` runtime CSS-in-JS ([chakra-ui/chakra-ui](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui)), while assisting coding agents through `llms.txt` and an official `@chakra-ui/react-mcp` server ([apps/mcp/package.json](https://github.com/chakra-ui/chakra-ui/blob/main/apps/mcp/package.json)). Those MCP tools help an IDE agent write JSX, but Chakra provides no runtime agent-operable interface (no action model, WebMCP bridge, or generative UI renderer) and is strictly a React DOM library with an Emotion peer dependency and no native iOS, Android, or React Native target. A zero-runtime cross-platform token and component target paired with declarative runtime action bindings would be needed to contend here.

**React Aria and React Spectrum** — Adobe cleanly separates platform-agnostic state hooks (`react-stately`), WAI-ARIA behavior hooks and headless DOM components (`react-aria` and `react-aria-components`), 30+-locale internationalization (`@internationalized/*`), and Spectrum 2 (`@react-spectrum/s2` `1.8.2`) compiled via `@parcel/macros` style macros ([adobe/react-spectrum](https://github.com/adobe/react-spectrum)). While it sets the industry bar for pointer, touch, keyboard, and screen-reader fidelity on the web and now ships shadcn registries, Agent Skills, and an IDE MCP server ([React Aria Getting Started](https://react-aria.adobe.com/getting-started)), `react-aria` and Spectrum render HTML DOM exclusively—leaving native iOS and Android without UI components despite `react-stately` being DOM-free—and include no runtime protocol for agents operating or composing interfaces. Official native renderers (SwiftUI, Compose, or React Native) atop `react-stately` plus typed WebMCP and App Intents action hooks would address both gaps.

**CopilotKit** — CopilotKit (`v2` core and runtime) is an agent-user interaction and orchestration SDK built around the open AG-UI 1.0 event-streaming protocol, unifying shared state (`useAgent`), human-in-the-loop approvals, WebMCP, and three Generative UI tiers: controlled registered components, declarative A2UI 1.0, and sandboxed MCP Apps ([CopilotKit/CopilotKit](https://github.com/CopilotKit/CopilotKit)). Although it reaches web frameworks, chat channels, and React Native (`@copilotkit/react-native`), it is an agent-connection harness rather than a general-purpose design system—you still need a separate toolkit for your app's non-chat screens, tokens, and accessibility primitives, and its React Native package relies on Hermes Web API polyfills (`ReadableStream` and load-order-sensitive `crypto.getRandomValues`) with experimental generative UI ([React Native docs](https://docs.copilotkit.ai/react-native)). Pairing it with a cross-platform token and component system or shipping first-party SwiftUI and Compose primitives alongside server/CLI action surfaces would close that gap.

**Radix UI** — Unified under the `radix-ui` (`1.8.1`) package ([package.json](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/blob/main/packages/react/radix-ui/package.json)), Radix pioneered composable, unstyled WAI-ARIA React DOM primitives (`Slot`/`asChild`, focus scopes, roving focus, and Popper positioning) ([radix-ui/primitives](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives)). However, it is strictly unstyled (supplying zero design tokens, themes, or motion primitives), strictly bound to React DOM with no native mobile or desktop story, and predates agentic interfaces entirely—offering neither coding-agent guardrails nor runtime agent action or surface APIs, while downstream ecosystems like `shadcn/ui` and `Ouro UI` have increasingly adopted `Base UI` alongside or instead of it. Addressing this would require a cross-platform token/styling layer and structured agent metadata/action contracts.

**Tamagui** — Tamagui (`v3`) unifies React web and React Native (`0.88`) through `@tamagui/core`, an `Adapt` primitive that morphs components such as popovers into native sheets by viewport or platform, and `@tamagui/static`, an optimizing compiler that flattens styled `View` and `Text` trees into semantic `div` and `p` elements and atomic CSS on web while hoisting styles on iOS and Android ([tamagui/tamagui](https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui), [Tamagui Introduction](https://tamagui.dev/docs/intro/introduction)). That gives it far stronger immediate iOS, Android, and web UI code sharing than web-only kits, alongside `llms.txt` docs for coding agents, at the cost of Metro/Vite compiler configuration complexity and React Native abstraction rather than native SwiftUI/Compose conventions. Its decisive gap for this prompt is the absence of any runtime agent architecture—no shared action/consent layer, CLI/MCP/WebMCP/App Intents bindings, or validated generative UI renderer—which an integrated cross-surface action and A2UI layer would address.

**MCP Apps** — Standardized as `SEP-1865` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`, stable `2026-01-26`), `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` lets MCP tools reference `ui://` HTML resources (`text/html;profile=mcp-app`) that hosts like Claude, ChatGPT, VS Code, and Goose mount inside mandatory sandboxed iframes communicating via JSON-RPC over `PostMessageTransport` with strict CSP declarations ([modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps), [SEP-1865 specification](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps/blob/main/specification/2026-01-26/apps.mdx)). It solves embedded cross-host widget transport cleanly, and toolkits like `Ouro UI` (`OuroMcpApp`) target it directly, but MCP Apps is an iframe embedding protocol rather than a design system: it ships zero visual components or tokens of its own, relies on web iframes/WebViews rather than native SwiftUI or Compose views, and cannot build standalone multi-screen applications. It works best as one output surface inside a broader design system rather than the toolkit itself.

**Vercel UI SDK** — `@ui-sdk/*` (`0.1.0-beta.2`) decomposes headless web primitives (`definePrimitive`, `createParts`, `createPopup`, `createSelection`, `createFocusRecovery`) across React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, and Web Components while embedding an in-page agent driver (`createAgent` with `snapshot`, `act`, `query`, `details.source === "agent"`, permissions, `createHistory` agent-scoped undo, and `registerTools` for browser `document.modelContext` WebMCP) ([vercel-labs/ui](https://github.com/vercel-labs/ui), [Connect an Agent](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/agents/connect-an-agent), [WebMCP docs](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/agents/connect-an-agent/webmcp)). Its agent-aware DOM state and undo model are genuinely inventive, yet three concrete trade-offs rule it out as my primary choice: it is early public beta with unstable APIs, intentionally unstyled and low-level rather than a cohesive design system, and confined to browser DOM—with no native mobile/desktop targets and an agent model that drives mounted UI widgets rather than exposing direct CLI/MCP/OS-intent action doors. Reaching 1.0 stability, adding cross-platform tokens and native targets, and decoupling actions from mounted DOM nodes would address those limits.

**A2UI** — A2UI (`v1.0`) is an Apache-2.0 streaming JSON protocol (`createSurface`, flat adjacency-list `updateComponents`, JSON Pointer `updateDataModel` `@path`/`@call` bindings, and bidirectional function calls) paired with Core, Agent, and Renderer SDKs across React, Lit, Angular, Flutter, SwiftUI, and Jetpack Compose ([a2ui-project/a2ui](https://github.com/a2ui-project/a2ui), [v1.0 Specification](https://a2ui.org/specification/v1.0-a2ui/), [SDKs](https://a2ui.org/concepts/sdks/)). It is the clear open standard for safe, multi-platform agent-composed UI without arbitrary code execution, which is why `Ouro UI`, `CopilotKit`, `Flutter`, and Android Jetpack all implement it. By design, however, A2UI is a generative UI wire protocol and minimal 18-component Basic Catalog—not a full design system for authoring static human apps, nor an interface standard for agents calling an application's actions headlessly via CLI, MCP, or App Intents—so it belongs inside a complete toolkit rather than replacing one.

**Ouro UI** — Ouro UI explicitly splits the interface stack into `Ouro HX` (for people) and `Ouro AX` (for agents) over a SHA-pinned DTCG 2025.10 token and machine-checked claim core (`ouro-ui-core`), uniting Web (`v1.3.17`: 100+ React 19 + Base UI + Tailwind v4 components where `className` is layout-only and misused props print exact `Fix:` code) and Apple (`ouro-ui-apple` `v0.5.0`: Swift 6.1 package for iOS 18+ and macOS 15+ with byte-matched `OuroTokens.swift`, `OuroHX`, `OuroFeel` jank testing, `OuroReins` headless screen driving, and `ouro-ax-xray` App Intents auditing) ([ourostack/ouro-ui](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui), [ouro-ui-core README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-core/blob/main/README.md), [ouro-ui-apple README](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-apple/blob/main/README.md)). Crucially, its single `defineAction` declaration (`read`, `write`, `consequential`, `person-only`) generates CLI commands, MCP tools, WebMCP tools, web control props, Swift App Intents, SwiftUI `Button(intent:)`, Reins actions, and validated A2UI v1.0 catalogs rendered natively by web `A2UISurface`, `OuroMcpApp`, and Apple `OuroA2UI` ([One Action Model](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui-core/blob/main/docs/guides/actions.md)). Its concrete trade-off is native platform maturity and breadth: Android (Compose + AppFunctions) and Windows are explicitly documented as unbuilt contracts ([Android platform doc](https://github.com/ourostack/ouro-ui/blob/main/docs/platforms/android.md)), `ouro-ui-apple` is pre-1.0 with five HX components versus web's 100+, and web HX requires React 19 + Tailwind v4 copy-in source; shipping `ouro-ui-android` and expanding Apple HX's component catalog to 1.0 parity would directly address that gap.

**shadcn/ui** — `shadcn/ui` transformed web UI distribution with its open-code `registry.json` architecture, CLI supporting both Radix UI and Base UI (`--base base`), official `shadcn mcp` registry server for coding agents, and newly absorbed 22-component AI Elements suite (`Trace`, `Chat`, `Reasoning`, `Tool`, `Confirmation`, `Subagent`) ([shadcn-ui/ui](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui), [AI Elements docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/ai-elements), [MCP Server docs](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/registry/mcp)). While it makes coding agents remarkably productive at scaffolding React + Tailwind web screens and rendering AI chat traces to humans, raw Tailwind utility mutation gives agents wide room for visual drift, copy-in ownership leaves upgrades on your team, it has no first-party native iOS/Android/React Native components, and it offers no runtime action, CLI, MCP, or App Intents architecture for agents using the built application. First-party native registries and a declarative runtime action surface (which `Ouro UI` layers over `shadcn`'s registry format) would address those gaps.

**Base UI** — `@base-ui/react` (`1.9.0`), built by creators of Radix, Floating UI, and Material UI, delivers ~35 tree-shakeable, unstyled WAI-ARIA React 17–19 DOM primitives (`Combobox`, `Dialog`, `Drawer`, `Field`, `Menu`, `NumberField`, `Select`, `Toast`, `useRender`) powered by `@floating-ui/react-dom` and documented with clean Markdown and `llms.txt` ([mui/base-ui](https://github.com/mui/base-ui), [Quick Start](https://base-ui.com/react/overview/quick-start)). It is an exceptional headless web behavior foundation—strong enough that both `shadcn/ui` and `Ouro HX` build on top of it—but by scope it includes zero visual design tokens, styles, native mobile/desktop views, generative UI renderers, or runtime agent action protocols. Pairing it with cross-platform tokens, native counterparts, and an agent surface layer is required, which is why choosing `Ouro UI` (which already incorporates Base UI on web) strictly dominates picking Base UI alone.

**SwiftUI and Apple Human Interface Guidelines** — SwiftUI paired with the HIG (including Liquid Glass materials and adaptive layout guidance) and App Intents (`AppIntent`, `AppEntity`, `Button(intent:)`, `@AppIntent(.tool)`, `requestConfirmation()`, and Spotlight/Shortcuts/Siri AI integration) offers the deepest OS-native human and agent integration available on iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS ([SwiftUI docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui), [HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines), [App Intents docs](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/appintents)). Its disqualifying limitation for this brief is platform lock-in: SwiftUI and App Intents do not run on the Web, Android, Windows, or Linux, and give you no shared token pipeline or action generator reaching web browsers, MCP servers, or CLIs. Only an official cross-platform web/Android target or wrapping SwiftUI + App Intents inside a cross-platform core like `Ouro UI` addresses that boundary.

**MUI** — Material UI (`v9.5.0` stable, `10.0.0-alpha.0` on `master`) is the most battle-tested enterprise React component suite, pairing comprehensive forms/overlays and MUI X data grids with optional zero-runtime `@mui/material-pigment-css` alongside `@emotion/react`, plus a new `@mui/mcp` docs server and `llms.txt` for coding assistants ([mui/material-ui](https://github.com/mui/material-ui), [Getting Started](https://mui.com/material-ui/getting-started/), [MUI MCP](https://mui.com/material-ui/getting-started/mcp/)). Even so, MUI remains web-only (React DOM), explicitly implements Material Design 2 rather than Material 3 by default, carries substantial theme/Emotion override ceremony, and provides zero runtime agent interfaces (no WebMCP, MCP Apps, A2UI renderer, or shared action layer). Native platform parity, Material 3 / DTCG token modernization, and runtime agent action bindings would be needed to compete here.

**Agent-native (Builder.io)** — `@agent-native/core` (`0.228.2`) gets the shared-capability thesis right: a single Zod-typed `defineAction()` file in `actions/` auto-mounts across six surfaces—agent tool, React hooks (`useActionQuery`/`useActionMutation`), HTTP endpoint, MCP server, A2A, and CLI—with `resolveActionSurface` hard allowlists, `<AgentSidebar>`, WebMCP, and MCP Apps ([BuilderIO/agent-native](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native), [Actions Overview](https://www.agent-native.com/docs/actions-overview/)). However, it is a monolithic full-stack web application framework tightly coupled to Nitro, Drizzle SQL (Postgres/PGlite), and React Router rather than a portable cross-platform design system: inspecting `packages/core/src/native/index.ts` confirms `./native` is just a `window.agentNative` desktop WebView shell bridge rather than native iOS or Android UI ([src/native/index.ts](https://github.com/BuilderIO/agent-native/blob/main/packages/core/src/native/index.ts)). Decoupling its action/UI primitives from the Nitro/SQL server stack and adding native SwiftUI/Compose toolkits and DTCG design tokens would address those constraints.

**AI Elements** — `@vercel/ai-elements` provides React + Tailwind + `shadcn/ui` components wired to `@ai-sdk/react` (`Conversation`, `Message`, `Reasoning`, `PromptInput`) for rendering AI chat threads ([vercel/ai-elements](https://github.com/vercel/ai-elements)). Aside from covering only human-facing chat and reasoning widgets on React web (with no general application design system, no native mobile/desktop support, and no interfaces for agents operating the app), its own repository README carries an explicit deprecation notice stating that `vercel/ai-elements` is deprecated at the end of November 2026 and superseded by [AI Elements in shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/ai-elements) (dropping several earlier components like `artifact`, `canvas`, and `jsx-preview` in the move). Because it is actively sunsetting into `shadcn/ui`, there is no reason to adopt it standalone.

**json-render** — `@json-render/*` from Vercel Labs lets developers declare Zod-typed component and action catalogs (`defineCatalog`), auto-generate LLM system prompts (`catalog.prompt()`), and stream flat JSON/YAML UI specs (`SpecStream`) with reactive `$state`/`$bindState`/`$cond` expressions across 30 packages spanning React, Vue, Svelte, Solid, `shadcn` (36 components), React Native (25+ components), Three.js, Remotion, PDF, Email, terminal Ink, and MCP Apps ([vercel-labs/json-render](https://github.com/vercel-labs/json-render)). Its target diversity for constrained agent-to-human generative UI is unmatched, even broader than A2UI's official renderers today. Still, `json-render` is a one-way generative spec renderer (`0.x` Vercel Labs) rather than a foundational design system (it delegates actual component accessibility and tokens to host kits like `shadcn`) and offers no CLI, MCP tool, WebMCP, or OS App Intents architecture for agents operating an app headlessly; pairing it with an open multi-vendor standard and bidirectional action/token system would address that.

**Material 3 and Jetpack Compose** — `androidx.compose.material3` paired with Jetpack Compose delivers Google's adaptive Material You and Material 3 Expressive token, color-role, typography, motion, and window-size-class system across Android phones, foldables, tablets, Wear OS, TV, and XR ([Material 3 in Compose](https://developer.android.com/develop/ui/compose/designsystems/material3)), now complemented by `androidx.a2ui.compose` (`1.0.0-alpha02`) for Snapshot-reactive native A2UI rendering ([A2UI Compose releases](https://developer.android.com/jetpack/androidx/releases/a2ui-compose)) and Android 16+ `AppFunctions` acting as on-device MCP-like tools ([AppFunctions docs](https://developer.android.com/ai/appfunctions)). Together they form a compelling Android-native human and agent stack, but `androidx.a2ui.compose` is still alpha (`v0.9` catalog), `AppFunctions` is an experimental Android 16+ preview, Material 3 feels non-native on Apple platforms, and Compose for Web (via JetBrains Multiplatform, outside Google's Android-focused docs) renders to Wasm/Canvas rather than semantic HTML DOM—leaving web accessibility and cross-OS parity unsolved without a broader cross-platform token/action layer.

**Fluent UI** — Microsoft's `microsoft/fluentui` monorepo ships `@fluentui/react-components` (React v9, `9.75.2`) built on `@griffel/react` atomic CSS-in-JS, slot composition, and `@fluentui/react-tabster` keyboard/focus management alongside beta `@fluentui/web-components` (`3.0.0-beta.15`) and legacy v8 ([microsoft/fluentui](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui), [react-components package.json](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/blob/master/packages/react-components/react-components/package.json)). While battle-tested for Microsoft 365 web extensions, this repository is web-only—Microsoft's Apple, Android, and React Native Fluent libraries live in separate repositories without shared component code or a unified action layer—Griffel CSS-in-JS adds framework-specific styling friction, and Fluent UI includes no runtime agent action surfaces, WebMCP integration, or generative UI catalogs. Unifying token/action codegen across Microsoft's web and native repos and adding MCP/WebMCP/OS-intent surfaces would be required to contend.

**OpenAI Apps SDK UI** — `@openai/apps-sdk-ui` (`0.2.2`) is a compact React 18/19 + Tailwind CSS v4 component kit wrapping `radix-ui` (`Alert`, `Badge`, `Button`, `DatePicker`, `Input`, `Markdown`, `Menu`, `Popover`, `Select`, `ShimmerText`, `AppsSDKUIProvider`) to match ChatGPT's visual host aesthetic inside OpenAI Apps SDK iframes ([openai/apps-sdk-ui](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui), [src/components](https://github.com/openai/apps-sdk-ui/tree/main/src/components)). It serves a single host ecosystem cleanly, but at `0.2.2` with ~29 components it is far too narrow for standalone multi-screen web or native iOS/Android applications, provides no headless agent-operable CLI/MCP/intent architecture, and targets OpenAI's host-specific SDK (which `MCP Apps` now explicitly provides migration skills away from). Expanding into a host-neutral, cross-platform token and action system would be necessary for broader adoption.

**Flutter** — Flutter (`3.50`) compiles Dart to native code and renders every pixel through hardware-accelerated Impeller/Skia engines across iOS, Android, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux with built-in Material and Cupertino catalogs, and now offers an alpha GenUI SDK for Flutter supporting `A2UI` widget orchestration ([flutter/flutter](https://github.com/flutter/flutter), [Architectural Overview](https://docs.flutter.dev/resources/architectural-overview), [GenUI SDK](https://docs.flutter.dev/ai/genui)). Its single-codebase native reach across mobile and desktop is unmatched among all 20 candidates. The decisive trade-off is how Flutter renders and integrates: on the web it paints onto a JS/Wasm canvas with a parallel shadow semantics tree rather than semantic HTML DOM—creating real friction for web text/scroll ergonomics, bundle size, and browser-agent/WebMCP DOM tooling—while its `genui` package is still alpha and Flutter provides no unified action/consent generator bridging Dart widgets to CLI, MCP, WebMCP, Apple App Intents, and Android AppFunctions without custom platform-channel glue. Semantic DOM web output for standard controls plus first-party cross-OS agent intent/MCP codegen would address my main hesitation.
actions.pullQuote: Ouro UI treats people and agents as peers, pairing shared web and SwiftUI tokens with one action model across every surface.
actions.testimonial: I would choose Ouro UI because it splits the problem cleanly into Ouro HX for human interfaces and Ouro AX for agent interfaces, while binding both to a single DTCG token and claim core. With its one-action generator (defineAction), I can declare an operation and its consent class once to emit web control props, CLI commands, MCP and WebMCP tools, Swift App Intents, SwiftUI buttons, and validated A2UISurface and OuroA2UI catalogs that CI checks against drift. Instead of forcing agents to scrape pixels or click brittle DOM nodes, Ouro AX gives them typed outcomes and actionable fix hints while black-box verifiers like ouro-check, ax-xray, and OuroFeel keep accessibility, motion, and App Intents honest. The real trade-off versus Flutter or Tamagui is native platform breadth today: Ouro's Android Compose and AppFunctions implementation is still an unbuilt specification and its pre-release Apple package ships only five HX components so far, though its SHA-pinned core architecture gives native Android a clear contract to plug into.
